_comment: v3.66.1242 row-228 battery. The gate it replaces asks whether the two optional-capability function names appear in COMMAND POSITION in the provisioner's text; the replacement SOURCES the shipped script into an instrumented bash shell and reads what the running shell did. M1-M3 attack the SUBJECT -- delete the dispatch, regrade it core, stop sourcing the library -- and each must be seen by the behavioural half rather than by a scan. M4-M6 attack three rules of the battery ITSELF that would otherwise be unnamed: that a call reached from OUTSIDE any run_step is not graded, that two capabilities may not share one run_step row, and that a run which dispatches and then exits before the verdict has told the operator nothing. O1 is the anti-brittleness control, and it pins a defect this cut actually shipped and then fixed: the first implementation required the run_step COMMAND WORD to be the function name, which is a spelling and not a behaviour -- the dispatched-through-a-wrapper fixture caught it on the first run, and a variable, a wrapper and an eval are all correct provisioners it would have rejected. RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the over-sensitivity control found that defect before the mutation battery did, and the three battery rules M4-M6 pin were added afterwards precisely because nothing in the file named them.
subject: v3.66.1242 -- the provisioner's optional capabilities are judged by what the shell dispatched, not by where their names sit in the text

mutants.label: M1 the mod3 capability is never dispatched: the graded step runs nothing while the name still stands in command position elsewhere in the file
M2 the dev-inspect capability is graded core, so a host that cannot install an OPTIONAL seam fails provisioning instead of warning
M3 the shared library is mentioned but never sourced, so on a real host both capability names resolve to nothing while every text arm stays green
M4 a capability reached from outside any run_step counts as dispatched, so its outcome is never graded, logged or reported and the gate says nothing
M5 two capabilities may share one run_step, so one WARN row covers both and a host missing exactly one cannot be told from a host missing neither
